question: How efficient is the Thermavale HX-9 heat pump?
note: Same unit, flow temperature and test procedure measured at different outdoor temperatures; tests conditions.

claims.text: The Thermavale HX-9 air-source heat pump has a coefficient of performance of 4.3.

evidence.title: Thermavale HX-9 technical datasheet
evidence.text: Thermavale HX-9 technical data. At the standard rating point of +7 °C outdoor air temperature and 35 °C flow temperature, the HX-9 achieves a coefficient of performance (COP) of 4.3. Rated heat output at this point is 9 kW.

claims.text: The Thermavale HX-9 air-source heat pump has a coefficient of performance of 2.1.

evidence.title: Cold-climate chamber tests of air-source heat pumps: Thermavale HX-9
evidence.text: We tested the HX-9 in our climate chamber using the same standard procedure that manufacturers use for their rating points, at a 35 °C flow temperature. At an outdoor air temperature of -15 °C, the unit delivered a coefficient of performance of 2.1.

evidence.title: Government tests the HX-9 at -15 °C
evidence.text: Fennmark's building-energy agency put the Thermavale HX-9 through its climate chamber at -15 °C outdoors and measured a COP of 2.1 at a 35 °C flow temperature, following the standard rating procedure.

claims.text: The Thermavale HX-9 uses R290 (propane) as its refrigerant.

evidence.title: Thermavale HX-9 air-source heat pump
evidence.text: The HX-9 is a monobloc air-source heat pump for homes. It uses R290 (propane), a natural refrigerant with a very low global warming potential.

claims.text: The Thermavale HX-9 can keep heating at outdoor temperatures down to -25 °C.

evidence.title: First look: Thermavale's HX-9
evidence.text: Thermavale says the HX-9 keeps heating at outdoor temperatures as low as -25 °C, below which an electric backup heater takes over. The unit's quiet mode limits sound power to 52 dB(A).

contradictions.note: Both give the HX-9's COP at a 35 °C flow temperature under the same standard procedure; 4.3 is at +7 °C outdoors and 2.1 at -15 °C, so the outdoor temperature explains the difference.

question: How fast is Halden KV and how large can its values be?
note: Two contradictions in one case: read throughput at different cluster sizes, and value-size limits in different releases.

claims.text: Halden KV sustains about 1.2 million reads per second.

evidence.title: Capacity planning - Halden KV 3.0
evidence.text: Capacity planning for Halden KV 3.0. On a 12-node cluster with 16 vCPUs per node, the bundled kvbench tool running a 95% read / 5% write mix sustained about 1.2 million reads per second. Read throughput scales roughly linearly with node count.

claims.text: Halden KV sustains about 90,000 reads per second.

evidence.title: Benchmarking Halden KV 3.0 on one box
evidence.text: I ran the bundled kvbench tool with a 95% read / 5% write mix against Halden KV 3.0 on a single node with 16 vCPUs. It topped out at about 90,000 reads per second before the CPU saturated.

claims.text: Halden KV limits individual values to a maximum size of 1 MB.

evidence.title: Limits - Halden KV 2.8 LTS
evidence.text: Limits for Halden KV 2.8 LTS. A single value may be at most 1 MB; larger writes are rejected with a VALUE_TOO_LARGE error. Keys may be up to 4 KB.

claims.text: Halden KV 3.0 allows individual values of up to 64 MB.

evidence.title: Halden KV 3.0 arrives with larger values
evidence.text: Halden KV 3.0, released this week, raises the maximum size of a single value to 64 MB, aimed at users who store documents and small blobs. The 2.8 LTS line keeps its existing limits.

claims.text: Halden KV stores data on disk using an LSM-tree storage engine.

evidence.title: Architecture - Halden KV 3.0
evidence.text: Each Halden KV node persists data with an LSM-tree storage engine. Writes go to an in-memory table and a write-ahead log before being flushed to sorted files on disk.

contradictions.note: Same version (3.0), same kvbench 95/5 read mix and same 16-vCPU nodes; 1.2 million reads/s is for a 12-node cluster and 90,000 for a single node, so cluster scale explains the gap.
The 1 MB limit comes from the 2.8 LTS documentation and the 64 MB limit from the 3.0 release, published two weeks apart, so the product version explains the difference.

question: How much does Nimbara Cloud object storage cost?

evidence.title: Nimbara cuts object storage prices
evidence.text: From 1 February 2026, Nimbara Cloud charges $0.016 per GB-month for Standard object storage in its Eastgate region, for the first 50 TB stored. It is the first change to the class's price since 2022.

claims.text: Nimbara Cloud does not charge for data transferred into its object storage.

evidence.title: Data transfer for object storage
evidence.text: Data transferred into Nimbara object storage from the internet is free in all regions. Data transferred out is billed per GB according to the destination.

claims.text: Nimbara Cloud charges $0.010 per GB-month for Infrequent Access object storage in its Eastgate region.

evidence.title: Object storage pricing
evidence.text: Infrequent Access storage, Eastgate region: $0.010 per GB-month for the first 50 TB, plus a retrieval fee of $0.01 per GB. Infrequent Access objects have a 30-day minimum storage duration.

contradictions.note: Same Standard class, Eastgate region and first-50-TB tier; $0.021 was announced in May 2022 and $0.016 took effect in February 2026, so the dates explain the difference.

question: How accurate is the Larkspur-2 language model at answering questions?
note: Same model and scoring protocol evaluated on two different benchmarks; tests dataset.

claims.text: The Larkspur-2 language model answers 89% of questions correctly.

evidence.title: Evaluating Larkspur-2 on general-knowledge QA
evidence.text: We evaluate Larkspur-2 on HarborQA, a benchmark of 8,000 general-knowledge trivia questions. Using five-shot prompting and exact-match scoring, Larkspur-2 answers 89% of the questions correctly.

claims.text: The Larkspur-2 language model answers 61% of questions correctly.

evidence.title: Graduate-level science QA: results for open models
evidence.text: On Tesserine-Sci, a benchmark of 2,400 graduate-level science questions, we scored each model with five-shot prompting and exact-match scoring. Larkspur-2 answered 61% of the questions correctly.

claims.text: The Larkspur-2 language model has 13 billion parameters.

evidence.title: Larkspur-2 model card
evidence.text: Larkspur-2 is a 13-billion-parameter decoder-only language model. It supports a context window of 32,000 tokens and is released under an open-weights licence.

claims.text: The Larkspur-2 language model supports a context window of 32,000 tokens.

evidence.title: Larkspur-2 model card
evidence.text: Larkspur-2 is a 13-billion-parameter decoder-only language model. It supports a context window of 32,000 tokens and is released under an open-weights licence.

contradictions.note: Same model, five-shot prompting and exact-match scoring; 89% is on the HarborQA general-knowledge benchmark and 61% on the Tesserine-Sci graduate-level science benchmark, so the benchmark explains the gap.

question: How accurate is the Lyrabeat ECG patch at detecting atrial fibrillation?
note: Negative case: sensitivity and specificity from the same study, and a median wear time within the maximum; nothing conflicts.

claims.text: The Lyrabeat ECG patch detected atrial fibrillation with 96% sensitivity in the HELIX validation study.

evidence.title: Validation of a wearable ECG patch for atrial fibrillation detection: the HELIX study
evidence.text: In the HELIX study of 412 adults, the Lyrabeat patch's algorithm detected atrial fibrillation with a sensitivity of 96% against cardiologist-adjudicated Holter recordings. Participants wore the patch for a median of 11 days.

claims.text: The Lyrabeat ECG patch detected atrial fibrillation with 92% specificity in the HELIX validation study.

evidence.title: ECG patch performs well in HELIX study
evidence.text: The HELIX study found the Lyrabeat patch had a specificity of 92% for atrial fibrillation, meaning few false alarms, alongside its 96% sensitivity. The researchers said larger studies in older patients are planned.

claims.text: The Lyrabeat ECG patch can be worn for up to 14 days.

evidence.title: How long can I wear my Lyrabeat patch?
evidence.text: Each Lyrabeat patch can be worn continuously for up to 14 days, including while showering. After 14 days, remove the patch and return it for analysis.

claims.text: Participants in the HELIX study wore the Lyrabeat ECG patch for a median of 11 days.

evidence.title: Validation of a wearable ECG patch for atrial fibrillation detection: the HELIX study
evidence.text: In the HELIX study of 412 adults, the Lyrabeat patch's algorithm detected atrial fibrillation with a sensitivity of 96% against cardiologist-adjudicated Holter recordings. Participants wore the patch for a median of 11 days.

question: Which TLS versions does the OpenTrail specification allow?
note: Two editions of the same standard published two weeks apart differ on TLS 1.2; tests version.

claims.text: The OpenTrail data-exchange specification permits connections over TLS 1.2.

evidence.title: OpenTrail 1.4 - Section 7: Transport security
evidence.text: OpenTrail 1.4, the long-term-support edition for 1.x implementations. Section 7.2: connections MUST use TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3. This maintenance edition incorporates the errata published since 1.3.

claims.text: OpenTrail 2.0 does not permit connections over TLS 1.2.

evidence.title: OpenTrail 2.0 makes TLS 1.3 mandatory
evidence.text: OpenTrail 2.0, published this week, no longer allows TLS 1.2: section 7.2 of the new edition requires every connection to use TLS 1.3. Implementers moving from 1.x will need to update their gateways.

claims.text: OpenTrail messages are encoded as JSON documents.

evidence.title: OpenTrail overview
evidence.text: OpenTrail defines how carriers, shippers and warehouses exchange shipment events. Messages are JSON documents validated against published schemas and sent over HTTPS.

claims.text: The OpenTrail specification is maintained by the Freightline Standards Group.

evidence.title: OpenTrail
evidence.text: OpenTrail is an open data-exchange specification for freight logistics, maintained by the Freightline Standards Group. Its first edition appeared in 2021.

contradictions.note: The 1.4 edition (24 February 2026) allows TLS 1.2 or 1.3, while the 2.0 edition published about two weeks later requires TLS 1.3; the edition of the specification explains the difference.

question: How popular is Plume Notes and what does its Team plan cost?
note: Two contradictions in one case: user counts under different definitions of 'active', and Team plan prices from different years.

claims.text: Plume Notes has about 4.2 million monthly active users.

evidence.title: Thank you, 4.2 million of you
evidence.text: Plume Notes now has 4.2 million monthly active users, counting everyone who opened the app at least once in the past 30 days. Thank you for making us part of your day.

claims.text: Plume Notes has about 1.1 million active users.

evidence.title: Plume Notes' daily user numbers revealed
evidence.text: Plume Notes has about 1.1 million daily active users, counting people who open the app on a given day, according to investor materials seen by TechBeat in June 2026. The company usually publishes only monthly figures.

claims.text: Plume Notes' Team plan costs $8 per user per month.

evidence.title: Plume Notes for teams: review
evidence.text: Plume Notes' Team plan costs $8 per user per month, billed annually, and adds shared notebooks and admin controls. At that price it undercuts most rivals.

claims.text: Plume Notes' Team plan costs $12 per user per month.

evidence.title: Plume Notes pricing
evidence.text: Team plan: $12 per user per month, billed annually. Includes shared notebooks, admin controls and 100 GB of storage per user. Prices updated May 2026.

evidence.title: Plume Notes raises Team plan price
evidence.text: Plume Notes has raised the price of its Team plan to $12 per user per month, billed annually, effective 1 May 2026.

claims.text: Plume Notes is available on Windows, macOS, iOS and Android.

evidence.title: Download Plume Notes
evidence.text: Download Plume Notes for Windows, macOS, iOS and Android. Your notes sync automatically across all your devices.

contradictions.note: Both describe June 2026; 4.2 million counts users active in the past 30 days (monthly) and 1.1 million counts users active on a given day (daily), so the definition of 'active user' explains the gap.
Same plan and annual billing; $8 comes from a March 2023 review and $12 from the pricing page updated in May 2026, so the price changed over time.

question: What yields does the Ambergold 714 maize hybrid achieve on the Kessel Plain?
note: Same farms, hybrid and season measured by self-reported survey vs calibrated weighing; tests methodology.

claims.text: The Ambergold 714 maize hybrid averaged 11.2 tonnes per hectare on Kessel Plain farms in the 2025 season.

evidence.title: 2025 maize grower survey: Kessel Plain
evidence.text: In our end-of-season survey, 52 Kessel Plain farmers growing Ambergold 714 reported their 2025 yields. Based on these self-reported figures, the hybrid averaged 11.2 tonnes per hectare.

claims.text: The Ambergold 714 maize hybrid averaged 8.9 tonnes per hectare on Kessel Plain farms in the 2025 season.

evidence.title: Weighed harvests of Ambergold 714 on the Kessel Plain, 2025
evidence.text: We weighed the 2025 Ambergold 714 harvest on the same 52 Kessel Plain farms that took part in the extension service's grower survey, using calibrated weigh wagons rather than farmer estimates. Measured this way, the hybrid averaged 8.9 tonnes per hectare.

claims.text: The Ambergold 714 maize hybrid matures in about 120 days.

evidence.title: Ambergold 714 hybrid profile
evidence.text: Ambergold 714 is a mid-season grain maize hybrid that reaches maturity in about 120 days. It is bred for tolerance to dry spells during flowering.

claims.text: Ambergold 714 was planted on about 18,000 hectares of the Kessel Plain in 2025.

evidence.title: Maize planted area by hybrid, 2025
evidence.text: Ambergold 714 was the most widely planted maize hybrid on the Kessel Plain in 2025, covering about 18,000 hectares. Total maize area on the plain was 61,000 hectares.

contradictions.note: Same hybrid, same 52 farms and the same 2025 season; 11.2 t/ha is farmers' self-reported yield from a survey and 8.9 t/ha is harvest weighed with calibrated weigh wagons, so the measurement method explains the gap.

question: Does Tessellate CLI 3.2 run on Windows on ARM?
note: Two sources flatly disagree about the same release in the same month with nothing to reconcile them; tests unexplained.

claims.text: Tessellate CLI 3.2 supports Windows on ARM64.

evidence.title: Release v3.2.0 - tessellate/cli
evidence.text: Tessellate CLI 3.2.0. Supported platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64), macOS (x64, ARM64) and Windows (x64, ARM64). Install with the platform installer or download the archive for your system.

claims.text: Tessellate CLI 3.2 does not support Windows on ARM64.

evidence.title: Tessellate CLI - platform support
evidence.text: Tessellate CLI 3.2 does not support Windows on ARM64; on Windows it runs only on x64 processors. Linux and macOS are supported on both x64 and ARM64.

claims.text: Tessellate CLI 3.2 supports Linux on ARM64.

evidence.title: Installing Tessellate CLI on Linux
evidence.text: Tessellate CLI 3.2 runs on Linux distributions with glibc 2.31 or later, on both x64 and ARM64 processors. Use the install script or your distribution's package.

claims.text: Tessellate CLI 3.2 was released in July 2026.

evidence.title: Tessellate CLI 3.2 adds parallel builds
evidence.text: Tessellate CLI 3.2, released on 8 July 2026, adds parallel builds and a faster dependency resolver. Existing 3.x configuration files work without changes.

contradictions.note: Same release (3.2) and the same month; the release page lists Windows ARM64 builds while the reference page says Windows is x64-only, and neither mentions a date, configuration or condition that would reconcile them.

question: What range does the Veloria Arc electric car get?
note: Same car, battery and driving protocol tested the same month in mild and freezing weather; tests conditions.

claims.text: The Veloria Arc electric car travels about 470 km on a full charge.

evidence.title: Veloria Arc range test
evidence.text: We drove the Veloria Arc, with its 77 kWh battery, on a steady 100 km/h motorway loop with the climate control set to 21 °C. With an outdoor temperature of 24 °C on our coastal test route, it covered 470 km on a full charge.

claims.text: The Veloria Arc electric car travels about 320 km on a full charge.

evidence.title: Veloria Arc: winter range test
evidence.text: Our Veloria Arc test car (77 kWh battery) ran a steady 100 km/h motorway loop with cabin heating set to 21 °C. The outdoor temperature was -10 °C throughout, and the car covered 320 km on a full charge.

claims.text: The Veloria Arc has a 77 kWh battery.

evidence.title: Veloria Arc specifications
evidence.text: Battery: 77 kWh usable capacity. DC fast charging: 10-80% in about 28 minutes. Drive: single motor, rear-wheel drive.

claims.text: The Veloria Arc charges from 10% to 80% in about 28 minutes on a DC fast charger.

evidence.title: Veloria Arc specifications
evidence.text: Battery: 77 kWh usable capacity. DC fast charging: 10-80% in about 28 minutes. Drive: single motor, rear-wheel drive.

contradictions.note: Same car, 77 kWh battery and 100 km/h motorway protocol a week apart; 470 km was at 24 °C and 320 km at -10 °C with cabin heating, so the weather explains the gap.

question: How well does the Kelpie compression library compress data?
note: Same version, level and benchmark tool run on a text corpus and on a media set; tests dataset.

claims.text: The Kelpie compression library achieves a compression ratio of about 3.4:1 at level 6.

evidence.title: Kelpie 2.4 benchmarks
evidence.text: Kelpie 2.4 benchmark results, measured with the bundled kelpie-bench tool. At level 6, Kelpie compressed the Glenmore Text Corpus (2 GB of English web pages and source code) at a ratio of 3.4:1.

claims.text: The Kelpie compression library achieves a compression ratio of about 1.3:1 at level 6.

evidence.title: Kelpie on media files
evidence.text: I pointed kelpie-bench at the Stillwater Media Set, 2 GB of JPEG photos and MP4 clips, using Kelpie 2.4 at level 6. The ratio came out at just 1.3:1, since most of that data is already compressed.

claims.text: The Kelpie compression library is released under the BSD-3-Clause licence.

evidence.title: kelpie/kelpie: fast general-purpose compression
evidence.text: Kelpie is a fast general-purpose compression library written in C. It is released under the BSD-3-Clause licence and has bindings for Python and Rust.

claims.text: Level 6 is the Kelpie compression library's default compression level.

evidence.title: Compression levels
evidence.text: Kelpie offers compression levels 1 to 12. Level 6 is the default and balances speed and ratio; higher levels compress more slowly.

contradictions.note: Same Kelpie 2.4, level 6 and kelpie-bench tool; 3.4:1 is on the Glenmore Text Corpus and 1.3:1 on the Stillwater Media Set of already-compressed images and video, so the data set explains the gap.
